title: Strength reduction + LFTR: a[i] on a running pointer
summary_caption: Multiply traded for one add per iteration, and LFTR retired the counter. In LLVM: IndVarSimplify canonicalizes, LSR strength-reduces.

frames.caption: The loop from §1: every iteration recomputes the address t = a + i*4 — a multiply just to reach a[i].
SCEV first: i starts at 0 and steps by 1 each trip around the back edge — the add-recurrence {0,+,1}. A basic IV.
And t = a + i*4 steps by 4 whenever i steps by 1: SCEV {a,+,4}. A derived IV — currently paid for with a multiply.
Strength reduction, step 1: materialize {a,+,4} as its own variable. Insert p = a in the preheader.
Step 2: keep p in step. Insert p = p + 4 beside i = i + 1 — from now on p always equals a + i*4.
Step 3: replace the use. The body loads straight through p — the per-iteration multiply is gone.
Only the exit test still reads i. LFTR, step 1: compute the bound in p-space once — pend = a + n*4.

set_labels.pre:
pre:
i = 0
p = a
pend = a + n*4

frames.caption: LFTR, step 2: retest against pend — p < pend replaces i < n. (LLVM goes further: icmp eq against the trip count.)
Now nothing reads i: delete i = 0 and i = i + 1. The counter is dead — the loop runs on p alone.
